channel.title: The Wobo blog
channel.description: What we learn while building a tutor, written down: how to read a syllabus document, what a board actually changed this year, and what a machine can and cannot do for a learner.

item.title: How to read a syllabus document and know it is current
item.description: Four checks tell you whether the syllabus in front of you is the one your board is actually setting this year, and all four take about five minutes.

item.title: What changed in the CBSE syllabus this year, with the document for each change
item.description: The middle stage is being taught out of new books with new chapter names, and two reading traps sit in the secondary documents. Each one cited to its page.

item.title: Why a drawn explanation lands where a finished diagram does not
item.description: A drawing carries the order the thinking happened in, and the order is most of the explanation. A finished picture has already thrown that away.

item.title: What to look for in a tutoring app, as the person paying for it
item.description: Seven questions worth asking of any tutoring app, why each one matters, and our own answers to all seven, including the ones that are not finished.

item.title: How a doubt gets solved from a photograph, step by step
item.description: What happens between photographing a page and understanding it, why the reading is shown back before any answer, and where this still fails.

item.title: What an AI tutor cannot do, said plainly
item.description: Eight things a machine tutor cannot do for your child, what we build instead of pretending otherwise, and the one thing it is genuinely good at.
